newsitem.title: USA: Barshefsky says Japan trade trend unacceptable.
newsitem.headline: Barshefsky says Japan trade trend unacceptable.

text.p: U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky took Japan's Trade Minister Shinji Sato to task over the recent trend of Tokyo's trade surplus, a Japanese spokesman said on Friday.
"Barshefsky told Sato that Japan's recent trade trend is unacceptable," the spokesman said.
Japan's trade surplus rose more than 200 percent in May after more than doubling in April.

Barshefsky was also quoted as saying a rise in Japan's external surplus with the U.S. to a level seen at a time when Bill Clinton became president cannot be accepted, the spokesman said. Barshefsky did not specify if she were referring to the surplus in Japan's current account or in trade.

Barshefsky pointed out that there are problems in Japan's car exports to the United States and in Japan's car imports from the U.S., the official said, adding she was apparently referring to a sharp increase in the exports and sluggish car imports.
She also argued that Japan's efforts to open markets to foreign glass and paper are not enough, the spokesman said.
